name: Mycosis Fungoides and Variants

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Society for Cutaneous Lymphomas (ISCL) Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of persistent, progressive, and/or patch/plaque-type skin lesions
Epidermotropic atypical T-cell infiltrate with cerebriform nuclei on skin biopsy
Loss of pan-T-cell markers (e.g., CD7) and clonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement
Detection of monoclonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement by PCR
Chronicity and progression of skin lesions over months to years

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions plus histopathological confirmation and immunophenotypic evidence of atypical T-cell infiltrate
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histological, and molecular findings due to overlap with benign dermatoses.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Plaque-stage lesions with indurated, raised borders

pathognomonic.notes: Clusters of atypical lymphocytes within the epidermis
searchTerms: small clusters of immune cells in skin biopsy

common.symptomName: Hypopigmented patches especially in darker-skinned individuals

common.notes: May indicate progression to tumor stage

occasional.symptomName: Tumor-stage nodules or tumors on skin
Hair loss localized to affected skin areas
searchTerms: hair loss in skin affected areas

rare.symptomName: Systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
searchTerms: general body symptoms like fever and sweating

rare.symptomName: Severe erythroderma covering >80% body surface area
searchTerms: red skin covering most of body

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear may show Sézary cells in advanced disease
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in progressive disease
imaging: CT scan for lymph node and visceral involvement staging
genetic: Clonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement detected by PCR
Loss of T-cell markers (CD7, CD26) on immunophenotyping
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating epidermotropism and Pautrier microabscesses
Flow cytometry of skin or blood samples for atypical T-cell populations

distinguishingFeatures: Histopathology shows regular acanthosis without atypical cells
Polymorphous inflammatory infiltrate without clonal T-cell population
Usually acute or subacute onset with pruritus
Presence of circulating malignant T-cells (Sézary cells) in blood

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions to tumor stage
Development of lymphadenopathy or systemic symptoms
Presence of circulating Sézary cells in peripheral blood
references: Willemze R, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005.
Guitart J, et al. Diagnosis and classification of mycosis fungoides. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2013.
Kim YH, et al. Mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome: Clinical presentation and staging. UpToDate. 2023.
